budget_items.topic: FY2026 LA4 rate changes by property class
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported year-over-year assessed-value changes from the new LA4 run, broken down by property type, noting single family was down slightly from earlier and condos, two-family and three-family properties also moved.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 new growth (real estate and personal property)
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor gave updated new-growth totals for real estate and personal property, which came in higher than the board's earlier estimate.
The assessor pushed back on the vendor's initial adjustment for one condo complex after checking sales herself, and the adjustment was reduced.

budget_items.topic: Site index cost changes by neighborhood
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reviewed how per-neighborhood site index costs shifted between fiscal years, noting most stayed flat while a couple of neighborhoods' costs dropped slightly and a large gap exists between two indexes.

A board member drafted a letter asking for stronger deadline enforcement in the vendor's contract, citing a past vendor problem in the assessor's office that was costly to fix once the company grew too large to be responsive.
The principal assessor said residents are seeing meaningful savings under the new means-tested senior exemption and more applicants are expected next year.
A board member described the newly introduced means-tested exemption for seniors and the number of applications received so far.
The board discussed a warrant article to raise the 41A income limitation, still awaiting town counsel's clarification on how many income categories the article covers.

budget_items.topic: Proposed property tax exemption for disabled residents
budget_items.what_was_said: Board members agreed to look into a future warrant article creating a property tax exemption for disabled residents, pending research into state limitations.
A board member described past revisions to exemption income and asset qualifiers that had gone unchanged for decades, citing an example threshold.

minutes.headline: Board interviewed a candidate for its vacant third seat and reviewed FY26 new-growth and rate data.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors interviewed a resident interested in filling its vacant third seat and answered his questions about the role, training, and appointment process. The principal assessor then gave a status report on FY2026 interim-adjustment data, new growth, and site-index changes, voicing frustration with the assessing vendor's late deliveries, before the board approved several sets of minutes, discussed a 41A income-limit warrant article, set future meeting dates, and voted to enter executive session on abatement and exemption applications.

what_happened.line: Board interviewed a resident for its vacant third seat but took no appointment vote.
Assessor reported FY26 new growth came in above the board's earlier estimate and flagged late deliveries from the assessing vendor.
Board voted to enter executive session to review abatement and exemption applications.
Board agreed to explore a spring warrant article creating a property tax exemption for disabled residents and is awaiting counsel on a 41A income-limit article.
Board approved minutes from three prior meetings, including an October 1 executive session.

why_it_matters: Who fills the assessors' vacant seat affects how property valuations that set individual tax bills get set and reviewed.
New-growth and site-index figures reported here feed into the FY26 tax rate calculation.
A disabled-resident tax exemption and a 41A income-limit change, if they proceed, would come to voters as warrant articles at a future town meeting.
